messages.content: Madison is next week, and the family just added a 10:30 Sunday brunch near campus. We already have the Friday afternoon one-stop, Sunday return, compact car, and west-side suite hotel. Can you run the final logistics pass?

Yes. Brunch still works, but treat noon as the departure time from downtown or campus. For Saturday, do not count on casual street parking near the ceremony; use the assigned ramp or official overflow/shuttle and arrive 75–90 minutes before doors. I’d also confirm flight times, rental desk hours, and seats today.
Friday arrival is 6:35 p.m. and the Sunday flight leaves at 4:40 p.m. Ceremony is 10 Saturday, doors at 9. Seat maps are open but I haven’t picked for either of us.

Friday should be fine if the bag is out by about 7:00; you can pick up the compact and reach the hotel around 7:45. Confirm the MSN rental counter is staffed past your arrival or has a real after-hours pickup. Sunday, leave brunch by noon, get gas near the airport, and aim to return the car by 2:45.
Hotel confirmed free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness. I still need the room request and Saturday parking plan.

Room request: quiet king suite away from elevators and ice, upper floor if available, Friday evening arrival noted, and easy parking for late check-in. For Saturday, prepay the ceremony ramp if offered. If not, use the official overflow lot and shuttle rather than circling campus.
Seats: should I chase two windows or keep us together? I care more about not splitting up.

Keep the pair together. Put you in the window and your spouse directly beside you if a pair is open; otherwise take the best adjacent pair in the same cabin. Screenshot both seat maps after selecting, then recheck the return at check-in in case the aircraft changes.
And a compact packing list? Graduation plus weekend, not a giant suitcase.

Pack one ceremony outfit, comfortable walking shoes, a light layer or rain shell, compact umbrella, brunch outfit that can reuse shoes, small card or gift, chargers, IDs, sunglasses, and a foldable tote for programs or family handoffs. Keep flight essentials and one change of clothes in the personal item. Add a Sunday reminder to gas the car before the airport.

messages.content: Graduation is off my plate. Next up is mid-June Central Texas: Monday equipment handoff in Round Rock, Tuesday training in north Austin, Wednesday clinic near New Braunfels, Thursday debrief probably San Antonio. I’ll have the rolling demo case. First pass?

I’d build this around the case, not rideshares. Before ranking it: are you willing to fly in Sunday, and is Thursday return required? The two big risks are a Monday-morning connection missing the 2 p.m. handoff and choosing a hotel that makes every loaded and unloaded stop annoying.

I can fly Sunday if it prevents chaos. There’s a Sunday afternoon nonstop Denver to Austin. Monday morning one-stop is cheaper but makes me nervous. Someone mentioned San Antonio first, but that seems backwards. I’m open on Thursday versus Friday for now.

Ranked first plan: 1) Fly into Austin Sunday afternoon nonstop, pick up a rental at AUS, and start from a north Austin/Round Rock base. It adds one hotel night but protects the Monday handoff and Tuesday 8 a.m. start. 2) Monday morning one-stop to Austin only if the handoff can slide; one delay creates a scramble with the demo case. 3) San Antonio first is weakest because you would backtrack north for Round Rock and north Austin before turning south again.
For hotels I saw a north Austin suite place, downtown Austin, and maybe a San Antonio final-night option.

The north Austin suite property is the best base for the first part: strong reviews, easier parking, pool and fitness, but no hot tub. Downtown Austin wins on dinner choices, but the parking cost and garage logistics are a bad match for a rolling case. If Thursday lands in San Antonio, I’d split the stay instead of forcing a late drive back to Austin.
How bad is keeping one hotel in north Austin the whole time?

Workable, but inefficient. Wednesday New Braunfels would be roughly an hour each way depending on traffic, and Thursday San Antonio can become 90 minutes each way. One hotel saves repacking; a split stay saves driving, lets you park once in San Antonio, and reduces the chance of arriving sweaty or late to the debrief.
I would rather not move twice. One move is fine. What car size?

Do one move. Rent at least a midsize SUV or small crossover, not a compact, so the demo case can lie flat and stay covered. Choose airport pickup and drop-off unless a city location is dramatically cheaper; the convenience is worth it with equipment.
What confirmations do I need from the clinics before we lock anything?

Ask for exact addresses, loading instructions, parking clearance or garage height, whether someone can receive the case if you arrive early, start and end times in writing, and whether Wednesday or Thursday supplies can be stored overnight. Also confirm the Thursday city and whether the debrief is near downtown, medical center, or the airport, because that affects the final hotel and return flight.
So what would you hold today without booking nonrefundable?

Hold refundable pieces: the Sunday afternoon Denver-to-Austin nonstop if the fare rules allow changes, a north Austin suite for Sunday and Monday nights, and a San Antonio-area refundable room for the last part once the debrief address is confirmed. Reserve a midsize SUV or crossover with AUS pickup and either SAT or AUS return left adjustable. Skip downtown Austin unless the Tuesday site moves there.

messages.content: The Central Texas times are firm now: Round Rock handoff Monday at 2, north Austin Tuesday at 8, New Braunfels Wednesday at noon, and a 1 p.m. San Antonio wrap Thursday. Help me make the booking calls.

That locks in the Sunday Austin arrival. The only real choice left is return timing: take a Thursday evening flight from San Antonio if it departs late enough, or add one San Antonio night and fly Friday morning. What return options are you seeing?

United has a Sunday afternoon DEN-AUS nonstop that lands around 5:40. For coming home I see a Thursday SAT-DEN at 6:55 p.m., or Friday morning around 9:30. Extra hotel night is reimbursable but I’d rather avoid it.

Book the Sunday nonstop into Austin and the Thursday 6:55 p.m. out of San Antonio. With a 1 p.m. wrap, even a 2:45 finish leaves time to get to SAT, return the car, and clear security. If that Thursday flight moves earlier than about 5:45, switch to the Friday morning plan.
Okay. On hotels, I had north Austin suite and the San Antonio medical-center hotel. How many nights at each?

Use two hotels, not three: north Austin Sunday and Monday nights for the Round Rock handoff and Tuesday 8 a.m. session. After Tuesday training, drive south and stay at the San Antonio medical-center hotel Tuesday and Wednesday nights. That makes New Braunfels a manageable Wednesday drive and keeps Thursday easy.
That means checking out before Tuesday training. Is that annoying with the case?

It is manageable if you set it up. Do mobile checkout or stop at the desk by 7:00, load the case into the covered cargo area, and park where you can easily access the vehicle. Do not leave anything visible. If the clinic has a secure room, bring the case inside; after training, drive straight south.
The north Austin hotel is well reviewed, pool and gym but no hot tub. San Antonio has pool, hot tub, fitness, and self-parking. Good enough?

Yes. The north Austin choice is location-first and still has the basics. The San Antonio hotel is better for recovery after the New Braunfels day, and self-parking matters more than a downtown restaurant scene on this loop.
Set the rental windows for me.

Reserve a midsize SUV or small crossover: AUS pickup Sunday at 6:00 p.m. and SAT drop Thursday at 5:00 p.m. Confirm the one-way fee, unlimited mileage, and whether a cargo cover is included or available. Add your flight numbers so the desk can see delays.
What notes go in before I hit purchase? Include seats and expense stuff.

Flights: choose a window seat on both legs if open, then screenshot the seats and fare rules. Hotels: request a quiet room not facing highway or elevators, with easy self-parking and elevator access; note late Sunday arrival in Austin and Tuesday evening arrival in San Antonio. Expenses: save the one-way rental fee, hotel parking, gas, and any clinic parking receipts; avoid prepaid nonrefundable rates. Calendar: add the Tuesday hotel move, Wednesday drive buffer, Thursday car return by 5:00, and a fallback reminder to revisit Friday morning only if the Thursday flight schedule changes.
